title: Production of E. coli-expressed Self-Assembling Protein Nanoparticles for Vaccines Requiring Trimeric Epitope Presentation
protocol: Mix 95 mL of component A and 5 mL of component B of the media in a 2 L sterile glass Erlenmeyer flask.
Add ampicillin to achieve a final concentration of 100 μg/mL.
Inoculate the media with E. coli from a previously established glycerol stock culture.
Incubate the culture at 30 °C with shaking at 200 rotations per minute (rpm) for 48 h.
Transfer the culture to two 50 mL conical tubes.
Centrifuge the tubes at 4,000 x g for 10 min with a fixed angle rotor at 4 °C.
Remove the supernatant and save the pellet to harvest cells.
Prepare imidazole-free buffer at pH 8.0 using 8 M Urea, 50 mM sodium phosphate monobasic, 20 mM Tris base, and 5 mM TCEP.
Filter the prepared buffer through a 0.22 μm vacuum bottle filtration unit.
Resuspend pelleted cells with 40 mL of imidazole-free buffer in a 50 mL conical tube.
Sonicate resuspended cells on ice for 5 min (4 s on, 6 s off) at 150 W output.
Centrifuge the cellular lysate at 29,000 x g at 4 °C for 25 min in a fixed angle rotor.
Transfer the supernatant to a 150 mL sterile flask and discard the pellet.
Dilute the supernatant to 100 mL with imidazole-free buffer.
Prepare Buffer A (imidazole-free buffer) by filtering through a 0.22 μm vacuum bottle filtration unit.
Prepare Buffer B (500 mM imidazole buffer) at pH 8.0 and filter it using a 0.22 μm vacuum bottle filtration unit.
Prepare isopropanol wash (20 mM Tris, 60% isopropanol) at pH 8.0 and filter through a 0.22 μm vacuum bottle filtration unit.
Equilibrate the His-column.
Open the FPLC software and click on the New method option.
Choose C1 port 3 from the drop-down menu for column position.
Select affinity from the Shown by technique drop-down menu.
Choose others, Histrap HP, 5 mL from the Column type drop-down menu.
Drag equilibration, sample application, column wash, and elution buttons in that order to the Method outline.
Set initial buffer B (4%), final buffer B (4%), and volume (CV) 5 for the equilibration phase.
Select Inject sample on column with sample pump in the sample loading box.
Check the Use flow rate from method settings box in the sample injection with system pump box.
Change the value to 20 mL next to the volume box on the right side of the screen.
Set initial buffer B (4%), final buffer B (4%), and volume (CV) 5 for the column wash phase.
Unclick the Enable box next to the fraction collection scheme.
Click on the elution button.
Set “initial buffer B” to 0%.
Set “final buffer B” to 100%.
Set “volume (CV)” to 5.
Enable fraction collection scheme.
Adjust fraction size to 4 mL.
Save the file as “equilibration”.
Connect a 5 mL prepacked His-column to column port 3.
Place pump A, pump B, and sample pump tubing into 0.22 µm filtered deionized water.
Run the equilibration program.
Replace tubing with imidazole-free buffer (Buffer A).
Run the equilibration protocol again.
Bind the sample to the column.
Purify the protein.
Open the FPLC software.
Click on the New method option.
Choose C1 port 3 from Column position drop-down menu.
Select affinity from Shown by technique drop-down menu.
Choose others, Histrap HP, 5 mL from column type drop-down menu.
Click on the Method outline button.

Drag the buttons from the Phase library popup menu: equilibration, sample application, column wash (Wash 1), column wash (Wash 2), column wash (Wash 3), and Elution next to the arrow in that exact order.
Close the Phase library menu.
Click on the Equilibration button.
Set “initial buffer B” to 4%.
Set “final buffer B” to 4%.
Set “volume (CV)” to 5.
Click on the Sample application box.
In the sample loading box, click the radio button for Inject sample on column with sample pump.
Check the box next to Use flow rate from method settings in the sample injection with system pump box.
Next to the volume box change the value to 100 mL.
Next to the fraction collection scheme click the Enable button.
Uncheck the Use fraction size from method settings box and then change the fraction size to 4 mL.
Click on the first column wash button (Wash 1).
Set “initial buffer B” to 4%.
Set “final buffer B” to 4%.
Set “volume (CV)” to 10.
Next to the fraction collection scheme click the Enable box.
Uncheck the Use fraction size from method settings and then change the fraction size to 4 mL.
Click on the second column wash button (Wash 2).
Set “initial buffer B” to 0%.
Set “final buffer B” to 0%.
Set “volume (CV)” to 5.
Enable fraction collection scheme for Wash 2.
Unclick Use fraction size from method settings.
Change fraction size to 4 mL.
Click on the third column wash button (Wash 3).
Set “initial buffer B” to 0%.
Set “final buffer B” to 0%.
Set “volume (CV)” to 5.
Enable fraction collection scheme for Wash 3.
Unclick Use fraction size from method settings.
Change fraction size to 4 mL.
Click on the Elution button.
Right click and delete step in the table.
Drag isocratic gradient button onto the table twice.
For the first entry, set “initial buffer B” to 30%.
Set “final buffer B” to 30%.
Set “volume (CV)” to 10.
For the second entry, set “initial buffer B” to 100%.
Set “final buffer B” to 100%.
Set “volume (CV)” to 10.
Enable fraction collection scheme for elution.
Click Save as button on top of the software.
Name file “purification”.
Place Pump A tubing into imidazole-free wash buffer.
Place Pump B tubing into 500 mM imidazole buffer.
Place sample pump tubing into 100 mL sample.
Run the “purification” program.
Pause the program at Wash 2, move pump A tubing to 60% isopropanol wash.
Restart the program to continue until isopropanol step completion.
Pause the program again and move pump A tubing back into the imidazole-free wash buffer.
Restart the purification program for automated continuation.
Combine flow-through fractions in a separate tube.
Combine Wash 1 fractions in a separate tube.
Combine Wash 3 (60% isopropanol) fractions in a separate tube.
Combine second set of Wash 3 fractions in another separate tube.
Do not combine elution step fractions with wash fractions.
Mix 15 µL from each pooled fraction and all elution step fractions with 2x Laemmli sample buffer.
Denature samples at 95 °C for 10 min.
Set up gel running apparatus with 3 stain-free 4–20% precast polyacrylamide gels in Tris-glycine SDS-PAGE buffer.
Load 8 µL of molecular weight marker to the first well.
Load 30 µL of denatured sample to other wells.
Run gels at 200 V until dye front hits bottom (about 30 min).
Rinse gels briefly with deionized water.
Image gels immediately using stain-free imaging system.
Identify fractions containing protein bands with the correct size (18.07 kDa).
Pool all identified fractions.
Run a western blot using an His-specific antibody and a SHB-specific antibody to identify the purified full-length protein.
Determine the protein concentration of flow-through, Wash 1, Wash 2 (60% isopropanol wash), Wash 3, and elution step fractions with spectrometer at 280 nm.
Generate dilutions containing 100 ng of protein in 15 µL imidazole-free buffer for each group.
Add 15 µL of 2x Laemmli sample buffer to each 15 µL of the samples.
Denature the samples as per step 4.1 instructions.
Spin down the tubes after denaturing to ensure all protein is transferred.
Load samples and pre-stained marker into a stain-free 4–20% precast polyacrylamide gel.
Run electrophoresis at 200 V until dye front reaches the bottom of the gel.
Make 1 L of TBS-T (20 mM Tris, 150 mM NaCl, and 0.1% Tween 20).
Make 200 mL of 5% non-fat milk in TBS-T.
Transfer protein onto a nitrocellulose membrane using a western blot transfer system.
Place the gel on the pre-assembled transfer stack.
Set up the system to run at 25 V for 7 min.
Check for the presence of the pre-stained marker on the nitrocellulose membrane indicating complete transfer.
Wash blots two times with TBS-T for 10 min each.
Block the nitrocellulose membranes (blot) with 5% non-fat milk in TBS-T for at least 1 h.
Wash blots two times with TBS-T for 10 min each.
Dilute the primary 167-D-IV antibodies to 1 mg/mL in TBS-T by adding 2 µL of stock Ab to 20 mL of TBS-T and diluting 10,000-fold.
Dilute the anti-6x HisTag antibodies to 1 mg/mL in TBS-T by adding 4 µL of stock Ab to 20 mL of TBS-T and diluting 5,000-fold.
Add the total 20 mL volume of primary antibodies, one to each blot, and incubate blots for 1 h.
Wash blots two times with TBS-T for 10 min.
Dilute 4 µL of 1 mg/mL mouse anti-human secondary antibody conjugated with alkaline phosphatase in 20 mL of TBS-T (1:5,000 dilution).
Dilute 4 µL of 1 mg/mL goat anti-mouse secondary antibody conjugated with alkaline phosphatase in 20 mL of TBS-T (1:5,000 dilution).
Add mouse anti-human secondary antibody to corresponding blots.
Add goat anti-mouse secondary antibody to corresponding blots.
Wash blots two times with TBS-T for 10 min.
Add BCIP/NBT alkaline phosphatase substrate to cover the blots.
Develop the blots for about 10 min until bands appear.
Rinse blots with cold tap water.
Let blots dry before scanning with a flatbed scanner.
Add pooled protein (10‒20 mL total) to a 10 kDa molecular weight cut off dialysis cassette.
Dialyze the sample into 8 M urea, 20 mM Tris, 5% glycerol, 5 mM TCEP pH 8.5 at RT (18‒26 °C) overnight.
Decrease the urea concentration in the dialysis buffer stepwise by 2 M every 2 h starting from 8 M to 2 M.
Move the dialysis apparatus to 4 °C when urea concentration reaches 2 M.
Stop using TCEP in the dialysis buffer at 2 M urea concentration and continue dialyzing at 4 °C until sample is in 120 mM urea, 20 mM Tris, 5% glycerol, pH 8.5 overnight.
Remove the refolded protein (SHB-SAPN) from the dialysis cassette.
Filter SHB-SAPN using a 0.22 μm PVDF syringe filter.
Aliquot SHB-SAPN into sterile tubes and freeze at -80°C, leaving at least 100 μL at room temperature for subsequent analyses.
Select protein as the material in the DLS software.
Create a complex buffer with 120 mM urea, 20 mM Tris, and 5% glycerol at 25 °C.
Select disposable cuvettes for analysis in the DLS software.
Set automatic measurement for 5 runs.
Add 45 μL of SHB-SAPN to a disposable cuvette.
Run the DLS software by clicking on the green arrow.
Select percentage volume for readout in the DLS software.
Dilute the sample by 1:20 in the refolding buffer for NTA analysis.
Make 10 mL of diluted sample.
Flush the NTA instrument with the refolding buffer using 3 mL syringes.
Load about 1.5 mL of sample to equilibrate the instrument for NTA analysis.
Create a new SOP in the NTA software by clicking on the SOP tab.
Change the number of captures to 3 and capture time to 30 seconds in the SOP.
Press the autofocus button on the left side of the screen for NTA analysis.
Fine-tune the focus using the manual focus knob on the side of the machine for NTA analysis.
Load a small volume of sample with the syringe when prompted by the system.
Wait for the system to capture all required images and bring up the analysis screen.
Slide the detection limit bar so that all real particles are marked with red crosses.
Press the run analysis button and wait for the analysis to begin automatically.
Prepare glow discharge formvar/carbon 400 mesh copper TEM support films.
Add 3 µL of sample at a concentration of 0.075 mg/mL to the grid for 30 s.
Wick off the liquid using filter paper.
Wash the grid with 3 µL of deionized water three times, wicking off each time.
Add 3 µL of 0.5% uranyl acetate to the support film and allow it to sit for 30 s.
Wick off most of the uranyl acetate but leave a thin film on the surface.
Allow samples to dry before imaging them on the transmission electron microscope.
Image samples at 80 kV on a TEM.
Remove kit and samples from refrigerator and allow to equilibrate to room temperature.
Write a program template so that wells are read every 150 s to identify onset time point (the OD increased by 0.2 in comparison with the first read).
Dilute the sample to the immunization dose concentration in PBS.
Resuspend the control endotoxin in an appropriate volume of endotoxin-free LAL water as determined by the certificate of analysis.
Vigorously vortex the vial for 15 min to ensure complete resuspension of the endotoxin.
Generate the endotoxin standard curve by performing a 10-fold serial dilution in glass vials ranging from 50 EU/mL to 0.005 EU/mL.
Add 0.1 mL of each previous dilution to 0.9 mL of LAL water for each dilution step.
Vortex vigorously after combination for 1 min.
Add standard curve dilutions and SHB-SAPN samples in duplicate to a 96-well plate.
Use LAL water as a negative control in duplicate.
Preincubate the plate at 37 °C for 15 min.
Resuspend the assay reagent vial with 2.6 mL of LAL water towards the end of incubation.
Gently mix content with a serological pipette.
Add 100 µL of the assay reagent to each well of the 96-well plate.
Quickly move the plate to the plate reader and run the program template.
Generate a standard curve using the log value of the controls versus the log value of the onset time.
Use the formula generated from this curve to calculate the endotoxin concentration in the samples.
